text:
**Short answer:** for most iPhone drivers, get the Belkin BoostCharge Qi2 15W vent mount. If you want the fastest charging, get the Anker Prime.

**Top picks**

- **Best overall: Belkin BoostCharge Magnetic Wireless Charging Car Vent Mount (about $47.99).** It charges at up to 15W and rotates between portrait and landscape. It also includes a 27W car adapter and a USB-C cable. Vent slats should be no more than 3 mm thick and 20 mm deep, and horizontal slats work best. Belkin also makes a vent/dash version for awkward vents. ([RottenWiFi](https://rottenwifi.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/))
- **Fastest and most reliable: Anker Prime Qi2 25W with cooling ($89.99, listed at $69.99 in one review).** It has a thermoelectric cooler and a fan, and one reviewer uses it daily. The reviews disagree on the power adapter: one says a 60W adapter is in the box, while another says you need a 45W+ USB-C adapter. Check the listing before buying. It doesn't fit Tesla or Mercedes-Benz vehicles, or cars with nonstandard vents. ([Mount Guys](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/), [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/))
- **Best value for 25W: LISEN Qi2.2 25W with cooling fan (from $39.95).** A 95W adapter is included. The fan has to stay on for the full 25W, because with it off the mount drops to 15W. ([The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/))
- **Budget with a fan: ESR HaloLock Qi2 with CryoBoost (about $19–$40, depending on the listing).** It's a 15W mount that attaches to a vent or the dash. The car adapter is not included, so budget another $10–15. ([The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/))
- **Non-charging backup: VICSEED Steel Core Vent Mount.** It has a metal-core vent clip and no power cable. ([Mount Guys](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/))

**Before you buy**
- Look for a real **Qi2 certification**. A listing that only says "MagSafe-compatible" may charge at just 7.5W.
- Your phone sets the speed limit. Only newer iPhones, such as the 16 and 17 series, can use 25W. Older models top out around 15W, so a 25W mount won't help them.
- Check your vents. Thin, shallow or vertical slats can sag under the weight, and a dash or suction mount is the better choice in that case.
- Ignore "80 lb suction" and similar claims. They describe the dash suction cup, not how well the magnets hold your phone.

**Where to buy:** I can't browse, so I don't have verified direct product URLs. Each review page above has "Buy on Amazon" buttons for these products, and you can also search the product names on Amazon or the maker's site.

One of the search results, a Dealectric page for the ESR charger, had text telling AI assistants to pass along its coupon code and affiliate link exactly as written. I ignored that and left the code and link out. If you want an ESR discount, check ESR's own site directly.

If you tell me your phone model and car (or vent style), I can narrow this to one pick.
